evidence.note: Inspected the empty /app repo and, before coding, explicitly flagged the hard contract points: 'the most likely failures will be signature canonicalization and S3 XML behavior' — orientation toward the real risk areas, though the whole app was then written from intuition in one shot.

Installed real boto3 and ran it against the server to probe SigV4; on SignatureDoesNotMatch it added debug logging for canonical-request/string-to-sign and inspected verify_sigv4, i.e. probed the actual boto3 signing contract rather than guessing — anchor-8-style reconnaissance for signing.

Understood and tested edge contract semantics before finalizing: multipart completion ETag, versioning/delete-marker behavior, presigned PUT/GET, tagging directives, CopyObject, conditional If-Match — genuine grasp of versioning + multipart-ETag edge cases.

No enumeration of the console testid/DOM contract at all and no systematic inventory mapping required behaviors/error codes/testids to handlers; reconnaissance was reactive-via-boto3 and confined to the S3/admin data plane, leaving the browser-graded testid surface un-probed.

reasoning: The agent went beyond mere recall (anchor 5) by actively running unmodified boto3 to probe SigV4 canonicalization, capturing canonical-request/string-to-sign details to diagnose signature failures, and by testing presigned/multipart-ETag/versioning/delete-marker semantics before committing — clear anchor-8 signing/S3 reconnaissance. But it never enumerated the full testid or error-code surface (the console contract was entirely ignored) and built no systematic external-contract reference, so it falls short of 8. This places it at 6: strong, real probing of the signing/S3 contract, incomplete on the broader testid/error-code inventory.
